name: Koh Phangan
tagline: Full Moon beach, quiet coves and jungle hills
summary: Known for the Full Moon Party at Haad Rin, but most of the island is quiet: yoga and sunsets on the west coast, remote coves in the north-east. Rent a scooter or use taxis and pick one coast as a base.
seasonNote: The Gulf islands are wettest from October to December, the opposite of Phuket and Krabi. Prices triple around each full moon.
arrival: No airport. Fly to Koh Samui and take a 30-minute ferry, or fly to Surat Thani and use a bus and ferry ticket (about 4 hours).
gettingAround: Shared songthaew taxis charge fixed, high prices; most visitors rent scooters, but the hill roads are steep and accidents are common.
cashTip: Bring cash for taxis, boats and markets; ATMs cluster in Thong Sala and Haad Rin.
foodTip: Eat at the Thong Sala night market, and look for southern curries and fresh seafood barbecues on the beach.
buyTip: The Saturday walking street in Thong Sala has crafts and clothes.
baseArea: Srithanu or Haad Yao for calm and sunsets; Haad Rin for the party; Thong Nai Pan for a remote beach
via: Via Bangkok to Koh Samui or Surat Thani

connections.note: Ferry to Samui or the mainland, then a flight.

items.name: Haad Rin and the Full Moon Party
items.summary: A crescent of white sand that hosts the monthly all-night beach party for up to 30,000 people.
items.expect: On party nights: loud, crowded and messy, with a 200 baht entry fee. On other days it is a pleasant, quiet beach.
items.tip: Check the date before booking; wear shoes on the sand and leave valuables in the hotel safe.
items.why: The island's famous event, and a good beach the rest of the month.
flow: Songthaew from Thong Sala, 25 minutes.
Sunrise Beach for the party; Sunset Beach to recover.
items.best: Full moon night, or any quiet morning

items.name: Thong Nai Pan beaches
items.summary: Twin bays, Noi and Yai, backed by jungle hills on the far north-east coast.
items.expect: A 40-minute drive over the hills; calm water and a small village.
items.tip: Thong Nai Pan Noi has the finer sand and better restaurants.
items.why: The island's most beautiful swimming beaches.
flow: Taxi or scooter over the paved hill road.
Swim, lunch in the village, walk between the two bays.

items.name: Bottle Beach
items.summary: A remote bay reached by longtail boat, with a few bungalows and no road worth driving.
items.expect: Boats stop running in rough seas.
items.tip: Take the longtail from Chaloklum rather than attempting the track.
items.why: The closest thing to the island as it was 30 years ago.
flow: Longtail from Chaloklum pier, 15 minutes.
Swim and hike to the viewpoint rock.

items.name: Haad Yao and Secret Beach sunset
items.summary: West-facing beaches with soft sand, clear water and sunsets over the Ang Thong islands.
items.expect: Small and popular; Secret Beach fills by late afternoon.
items.tip: Arrive by 4 pm and stay for a drink at a beach bar.
items.why: The best sunset spot on the island.
flow: Drive the west coast road from Thong Sala.
Swim, then watch the sun set.

items.name: Phaeng Waterfall and Domesila Viewpoint
items.summary: A jungle trail past a waterfall to a rock outcrop with a view over the south coast.
items.expect: A steep 20-minute climb on roots and rocks; the falls shrink in the dry season.
items.tip: Wear proper shoes and go in the late afternoon.
items.why: An easy taste of the forested interior.
flow: Park at the national park office.
Climb past the falls to the viewpoint.

items.name: Ang Thong Marine Park day trip
items.wiki: Mu Ko Ang Thong National Park
items.summary: A boat day among 42 limestone islands with kayaking, snorkelling and a steep viewpoint.
items.expect: A full day with an early start; the viewpoint climb is 500 metres of ropes and steps.
items.tip: Choose a speedboat for less travel time; the park closes in November.
items.why: The most dramatic scenery in the Gulf.
flow: Depart Thong Sala around 8 am.
Emerald lagoon, kayaking, viewpoint on Ko Wua Ta Lap.

items.name: Thong Sala Night Market
items.summary: The Phantip food market: dozens of stalls around shared tables, open every evening.
items.expect: Busy from 6 pm; cash only.
items.tip: Do a lap before choosing, then share several plates.
items.why: The cheapest and most varied dinner on the island.
flow: Arrive around 6 pm.
Order from several stalls and sit in the middle.

items.name: Fisherman's Restaurant & Bar
items.summary: A beachfront seafood restaurant with tables in old longtail boats.
items.expect: The best-known dinner on the island; full most nights.
items.tip: Reserve a table on the sand for sunset.
items.why: Fresh seafood cooked southern Thai style in a lovely setting.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Share a whole fish and a curry.

items.name: Bubba's Roastery
items.summary: A coffee roaster and all-day brunch cafe popular with long-stay visitors.
items.expect: Queues at weekend brunch.
items.tip: Go before 10 am.
items.why: The best coffee on the island.
flow: On the west coast road.
Brunch, then the beach across the road.

name: Koh Tao
tagline: Small island, clear water, cheap diving
summary: A small island built around diving and snorkelling. Many people come to get certified; everyone else snorkels the bays, hikes to viewpoints and takes the boat to Koh Nang Yuan.
seasonNote: November and December bring rough seas, poor visibility and cancelled ferries.
arrival: No airport. Ferries run from Koh Samui (2 hours), Koh Phangan (1 hour) and Chumphon on the mainland (2 hours).
gettingAround: Sairee and Mae Haad are walkable. Taxis are pick-up trucks at fixed prices; longtail boats reach the bays; roads to the east are steep.
cashTip: ATMs are in Mae Haad and Sairee; dive shops take cards with a surcharge.
foodTip: Roast duck noodles, beach barbecues and cheap Thai kitchens around Sairee.
buyTip: Little to buy beyond dive gear and beachwear.
baseArea: Sairee Beach for restaurants and dive schools; Chalok Baan Kao for quiet
via: Via Bangkok to Chumphon or Koh Samui

items.name: Koh Nang Yuan
items.summary: Three tiny islands joined by a sandbar, with a viewpoint and a coral garden.
items.expect: An entry fee, no plastic bottles allowed and crowds from 10 am to 3 pm.
items.tip: Take the first longtail from Sairee and climb the viewpoint before it queues.
items.why: The postcard view of the Gulf islands.
flow: Longtail from Sairee, 15 minutes.
Viewpoint first, then snorkel the Japanese Garden.

items.name: Scuba course or fun dives
items.summary: One of the cheapest and busiest places in the world to learn to dive, with sites like Chumphon Pinnacle.
items.expect: An Open Water course takes three to four days; standards vary between schools.
items.tip: Pick a school with small groups rather than the lowest price.
items.why: Diving is why the island is on the map; whale sharks pass from March to May.
flow: Classroom and pool on day one.
Four open-water dives over the next two days.

items.name: Sairee Beach
items.summary: The island's 1.7 km main beach, lined with bars, dive schools and leaning palms.
items.expect: Shallow at low tide; fire shows and music at night.
items.tip: The north end is quieter and best for sunset.
items.why: The social centre of the island and its best sunset.
flow: Walk the beach path from Mae Haad.
Sunset drink at the north end.

items.name: Shark Bay
items.summary: A calm southern bay where snorkellers often see green turtles and harmless blacktip reef sharks.
items.expect: Beach access is through resorts, some of which charge a fee.
items.tip: Snorkel in the morning at high tide and keep your distance from the turtles.
items.why: The best chance of seeing turtles without a boat.
flow: Taxi to Thian Og.
Snorkel out over the sea grass on the east side.

items.name: John-Suwan Viewpoint
items.summary: A rocky lookout over the twin bays of Chalok Baan Kao and Shark Bay.
items.expect: A short, steep scramble and a small entry fee.
items.tip: Pair it with Freedom Beach just below.
items.why: The best view on Koh Tao itself.
flow: Walk from Chalok Baan Kao, 20 minutes.
Climb, then swim at Freedom Beach.

items.name: Tanote Bay
items.summary: A boulder-ringed east-coast bay with good snorkelling straight off the beach.
items.expect: A very steep access road; take a taxi rather than a scooter.
items.tip: Snorkel around the big rock in the middle of the bay.
items.why: The best shore snorkelling on the island.
flow: Taxi over the hill, 15 minutes.
Snorkel, lunch at a bay restaurant.

items.name: 995 Roasted Duck
items.summary: A small shop serving roast duck over rice or noodles.
items.expect: A queue at dinner; shared tables.
items.tip: Go at off-peak hours and add extra duck.
items.why: The island's best-loved cheap meal.
flow: On the main Sairee road.
Duck noodle soup or duck on rice.

items.name: Barracuda Restaurant
items.summary: A seafood restaurant known for sharing platters of the day's catch.
items.expect: Busy every night in season.
items.tip: Book and order the seafood platter for two.
items.why: The most reliable seafood dinner on Koh Tao.
flow: Reserve ahead.
Platter to share, then dessert.

items.name: Su Chili
items.summary: A friendly Thai restaurant where the staff ask how spicy you want every dish.
items.expect: Popular with divers; quick service.
items.tip: Try the northern-style khao soi.
items.why: Well-made Thai classics at fair prices.
flow: In Sairee village.
Curry, a stir-fry and rice to share.

name: Pai
tagline: Mountain valley town with a slow pace
summary: A small town in a rice valley, three hours of bends from Chiang Mai. Days are for waterfalls, hot springs and the canyon; evenings are for the walking street.
seasonNote: March and April bring heavy smoke from field burning; June to October is green and rainy.
arrival: Minibuses from Chiang Mai take 3 hours over 762 bends; take motion-sickness tablets.
gettingAround: The town is walkable; the sights are 5 to 10 km out and need a scooter, a day tour or a hired songthaew.
cashTip: Mostly cash; ATMs are on the main street.
foodTip: Northern dishes such as khao soi, plus the widest choice of vegetarian food in northern Thailand.
buyTip: Handmade postcards, hill-tribe textiles and tea at the walking street.
baseArea: In town for the walking street; across the river for bungalows in the rice fields

connections.note: Hourly minibuses on a very winding road.

items.name: Pai Canyon
items.summary: Narrow red-earth ridges with steep drops on both sides and a wide valley view.
items.expect: No railings; some ridges are a metre wide.
items.tip: Arrive 45 minutes before sunset and wear shoes with grip.
items.why: Pai's best sunset.
flow: 8 km south of town.
Walk out along the first ridges and sit for sunset.

items.name: Wat Phra That Mae Yen
items.summary: A large white Buddha on the hillside above the valley, reached by 353 steps.
items.expect: Cover shoulders and knees.
items.tip: Go for sunset over the town.
items.why: The view across the whole Pai valley.
flow: 2 km east of the river.
Climb the steps to the Buddha.

items.name: Yun Lai Viewpoint
items.summary: A hilltop above the Chinese village of Santichon, known for a sea of mist at sunrise.
items.expect: A small entry fee that includes tea; cold before dawn.
items.tip: Be there by 6 am between November and February.
items.why: The valley filled with cloud at sunrise.
flow: Ride 5 km west before dawn.
Tea at the top, then breakfast in Santichon.

items.name: Tha Pai Hot Springs
items.summary: A forest stream fed by hot springs, with pools from 35 to 80°C.
items.expect: A national park fee for foreigners; the upper pools are too hot to enter.
items.tip: Go early in the morning in the cool season.
items.why: A warm soak in the woods on a cold morning.
flow: 9 km south-east of town.
Walk up to the source, then soak lower down.

items.name: Mo Paeng Waterfall
items.summary: A tiered waterfall with smooth rock that people slide down into the pool.
items.expect: Slippery rocks; low water from February to May.
items.tip: Best from July to November.
items.why: A fun swim stop beyond Santichon.
flow: 8 km west of town.
Swim in the lower pool.

items.name: Tham Lod Cave
items.summary: A river cave you cross by bamboo raft with a lantern guide, past ancient teak coffins.
items.expect: An hour's drive each way; a guide and raft are compulsory.
items.tip: Stay until dusk to see thousands of swifts fly in as the bats fly out.
items.why: The most memorable day trip from Pai.
flow: Drive or tour 50 km north-west.
Raft through three chambers with a local guide.

items.name: Pai Walking Street
items.summary: The main street closes to traffic every evening and fills with food and craft stalls.
items.expect: Busiest from 6 to 9 pm.
items.tip: Graze from one end to the other rather than sitting down.
items.why: It is where everyone in Pai ends the day.
flow: Start at the bus station end.
Snack your way down to the river.

items.name: Na's Kitchen
items.summary: A small family kitchen with a short menu of Thai staples.
items.expect: A wait for a table at dinner; opens in the evening only.
items.tip: Arrive when it opens.
items.why: The most recommended Thai food in town.
flow: Off the walking street.
Curry and a stir-fry to share.

items.name: Om Garden Cafe
items.summary: A shady garden cafe serving breakfasts, salads and cakes.
items.expect: Closes mid-afternoon.
items.tip: Good for a slow breakfast after a sunrise viewpoint.
items.why: The best brunch in Pai.
flow: Two streets south of the walking street.
Order at the counter and sit in the garden.

name: Sukhothai
tagline: The first Thai capital, by bicycle
summary: The ruins of the 13th-century capital sit in a quiet park of ponds and trees, far calmer than Ayutthaya. Rent a bicycle, see the central zone in a morning and the outer temples at sunset.
seasonNote: March to May is very hot; the Loy Krathong festival in November fills the park with lanterns and visitors.
arrival: Fly from Bangkok to Sukhothai airport (30 km away), or take a train to Phitsanulok and a one-hour bus. Buses from Chiang Mai take 5 hours.
gettingAround: Rent a bicycle at the park gate. A blue songthaew links the old city and the new town, 12 km apart, until early evening.
cashTip: Each park zone is paid separately in cash.
foodTip: Sukhothai noodles: thin rice noodles with pork, green beans, peanuts and lime, served dry or in broth.
buyTip: Sangkhalok ceramics, made here since the 13th century.
baseArea: The old city, near the park gate, for sunrise and sunset; the new town for more restaurants

connections.note: A few flights a day; 7 hours by bus.

items.name: Wat Mahathat
items.summary: The royal temple at the heart of the old capital, with a lotus-bud chedi and rows of columns around seated Buddhas.
items.expect: The largest site in the park; little shade.
items.tip: Be at the pond on the east side at sunrise for reflections.
items.why: The defining image of Sukhothai and a UNESCO World Heritage site.
flow: Cycle in from the main gate.
Walk around the central chedi and the standing Buddhas.

items.name: Wat Si Chum
items.summary: A 15-metre seated Buddha enclosed in a roofless hall, seen through a narrow slit in the wall.
items.expect: A separate ticket for the north zone.
items.tip: Go at opening when the light falls on the Buddha's face.
items.why: The most moving single image in the park.
flow: Cycle 10 minutes north of the walls.
Enter the hall and look up at the gilded hand.

items.name: Wat Sa Si
items.summary: A bell-shaped chedi and a seated Buddha on an island reached by a wooden bridge.
items.expect: Small and peaceful.
items.tip: The best sunset spot inside the central zone.
items.why: The prettiest setting in the park.
flow: North-west of Wat Mahathat.
Cross the bridge and circle the chedi.

items.name: Wat Si Sawai
items.summary: Three Khmer-style towers that began as a Hindu shrine before Sukhothai was founded.
items.expect: Quieter than Wat Mahathat.
items.tip: Look for the stucco figures high on the towers.
items.why: It shows the Khmer roots of the city.
flow: South of Wat Mahathat.
Walk through the hall to the three prangs.

items.name: Ramkhamhaeng National Museum
items.summary: Buddha images, ceramics and a copy of the Ramkhamhaeng inscription, the earliest Thai writing.
items.expect: A small museum; an hour at most.
items.tip: See it first to understand the walking Buddha style.
items.why: It gives the ruins their context.
flow: Beside the main gate.
Ground floor sculpture, then ceramics.

items.name: Wat Saphan Hin
items.summary: A standing Buddha on a wooded hill, reached by an old slate path, looking back over the city.
items.expect: A 10-minute climb on uneven stone.
items.tip: Come at sunrise or late afternoon.
items.why: The view of the whole plain from the Buddha's feet.
flow: Cycle 3 km west of the walls.
Climb the stone causeway.

items.name: Si Satchanalai Historical Park
items.summary: Sukhothai's sister city, with forest-wrapped temples and a chedi ringed by elephant statues.
items.expect: An hour's drive north; almost no visitors.
items.tip: Rent a bicycle at the gate and add the old kiln sites nearby.
items.why: Wilder and quieter than Sukhothai, and part of the same World Heritage listing.
flow: Bus or hired car, 55 km north.
Wat Chang Lom, Wat Chedi Chet Thaeo, then the hilltop temple.

items.name: Jay Hae
items.summary: The best-known shop for Sukhothai noodles, open from morning to mid-afternoon.
items.expect: Busy at lunch; closes around 4 pm.
items.tip: Order the dry version to taste the lime, peanut and palm sugar.
items.why: The reference bowl for the town's signature dish.
flow: On the road between the old and new towns.
One dry bowl, one soup bowl.

items.name: Ta Pui
items.summary: A rival Sukhothai noodle shop in an open wooden building.
items.expect: Daytime only.
items.tip: Add crispy pork crackling on top.
items.why: Many locals prefer it to its famous neighbour.
flow: A short walk from Jay Hae.
Small bowls, so order two.

items.name: Poo Restaurant
items.summary: A long-running traveller restaurant with Thai dishes, Sukhothai noodles and Belgian beer.
items.expect: Open in the evening when the noodle shops are shut.
items.tip: A handy dinner spot if you stay in the new town.
items.why: Dependable food and travel advice in one place.
flow: On the main street of the new town.
Noodles or curry with a cold beer.

name: Kanchanaburi
tagline: The River Kwai, the Death Railway and emerald falls
summary: A river town two to three hours west of Bangkok with a sobering wartime history and some of Thailand's best waterfalls. Give one day to the railway sites and one to Erawan National Park.
seasonNote: Waterfalls are fullest from July to November; March to May is very hot.
arrival: Trains from Bangkok's Thonburi station take 3 hours; minibuses and buses take 2 to 3 hours.
gettingAround: The town stretches 5 km along the river; use songthaews, a bicycle or a scooter. Erawan and Hellfire Pass need a bus, tour or car.
cashTip: National parks and trains are cash only.
foodTip: River fish, jungle curry (kaeng pa) and floating restaurants on the Kwai.
buyTip: Blue sapphires and gems from Bo Phloi are sold near the bridge; buy only if you know stones.
baseArea: Maenam Kwai Road for guesthouses and raft rooms on the river

connections.note: Two trains a day from Thonburi; minibuses are faster.
Minibus, sometimes with a change in Suphanburi.

items.name: Bridge over the River Kwai
items.summary: The steel railway bridge built by Allied prisoners of war and Asian labourers in 1943, still in use.
items.expect: You can walk across on the tracks; step into the bays when a train comes.
items.tip: Go early, or be there when the morning train crosses slowly.
items.why: The symbol of the Death Railway.
flow: Songthaew to the bridge.
Walk across and back, then along the river.

items.name: Death Railway train to Nam Tok
items.summary: A slow train along the original line, creeping over the wooden Wang Pho viaduct above the river.
items.expect: Two hours each way on wooden seats; a flat 100 baht fare for foreigners.
items.tip: Sit on the left side heading out for the viaduct and river views.
items.why: The most vivid way to understand what was built here.
flow: Board at Kanchanaburi or the bridge station.
Get off at Tham Krasae to walk the viaduct, or ride to Nam Tok.

items.name: Thailand–Burma Railway Centre
items.summary: A clear, well-researched museum on how the railway was built and what it cost in lives.
items.expect: Sobering; allow at least an hour.
items.tip: Visit before the bridge and the cemetery opposite.
items.why: The best explanation of the history anywhere on the line.
flow: Start upstairs with the route model.
Finish at the cafe overlooking the cemetery.

items.name: Kanchanaburi War Cemetery
items.summary: The graves of nearly 7,000 Commonwealth and Dutch prisoners who died building the railway.
items.expect: Immaculately kept and quiet.
items.tip: Read a few of the personal inscriptions.
items.why: It turns the numbers into people.
flow: Opposite the Railway Centre.
Walk the rows to the central cross.

items.name: Erawan National Park
items.summary: A seven-tier waterfall with turquoise pools you can swim in, linked by a forest trail.
items.expect: A 2 km climb to the top tier; fish nibble your feet; no food beyond tier two.
items.tip: Take the first bus at 8 am and walk straight to the top, swimming on the way down.
items.why: Among the most beautiful waterfalls in Thailand.
flow: Bus from Kanchanaburi, 90 minutes.
Climb to tier seven, swim at tiers five, four and two.

items.name: Hellfire Pass
items.summary: A rock cutting dug by hand, with a memorial museum and a walking trail along the old trackbed.
items.expect: 80 km from town; the audio guide is excellent and free.
items.tip: Walk at least to the cutting itself, 20 minutes from the museum.
items.why: The most affecting site on the railway.
flow: Bus towards Sangkhlaburi or a tour.
Museum, then down the steps to Konyu Cutting.

items.name: Wat Tham Suea
items.summary: A hilltop temple with a huge golden Buddha and tiered pagodas above rice fields.
items.expect: A steep staircase or a small funicular.
items.tip: Go late in the afternoon for the light over the paddies.
items.why: The best view near town and a striking temple.
flow: 15 km south-east by scooter or taxi.
Climb to the Buddha, then the pagoda next door.

items.name: Keeree Tara
items.summary: A terraced riverside restaurant looking straight at the bridge.
items.expect: Smart by local standards and busy at sunset.
items.tip: Book a river-edge table for the evening.
items.why: The best table view in town with good Thai cooking.
flow: Walk upstream from the bridge.
River fish and a jungle curry to share.

items.name: On's Thai-Issan
items.summary: A tiny vegetarian kitchen where On cooks on the street front and also runs cooking classes.
items.expect: A few tables and a fixed low price per dish.
items.tip: Ask about the two-hour cooking class.
items.why: The favourite cheap meal on the guesthouse strip.
flow: On Maenam Kwai Road.
Pick two or three dishes to share.

items.name: JJ Night Market
items.summary: An evening market beside the railway station with rows of food stalls.
items.expect: Mostly locals; cash only.
items.tip: Eat as you walk and finish with coconut ice cream.
items.why: The cheapest and liveliest dinner in town.
flow: Opens around 5 pm.
Skewers, noodles and sweets from different stalls.
